text: Novo Theatre, Dhaka (formerly known as Bhasani Novo Theatre and Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Novo Theatre), is a planetarium located on Bijoy Sarani Avenue in the Tejgaon area of Dhaka, Bangladesh. It opened to the public on 25 September 2004 and was initially named Bhasani Novo Theatre. The theatre was made autonomous through the Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Novo Theatre Bill 2010. The space center was commissioned by the Ministry of Science and Communication Technology of the Government of Bangladesh. On 20 March 2025, the interim government of Bangladesh, via an ordinance, changed the name of the planetarium from Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Novo Theater to Novo Theatre. Built on 5.46 acres of land, the planetarium features spaces ranging from a 21-meter dome seating 275 people to three-meter inflatable and portable domes where visitors sit on the floor. Designed by architect Ali Imam, the planetarium's dome simulates Earth with a cool blue sky and uses a 120-degree projection system to display moving images of planets and stars on a large-screen dome. Visitors do not need to look up; instead, they experience space as if they are living within it, thanks to 150 projectors. The facility offers three main exhibits: "Journey to Infinity," which presents stars, planets, and other celestial bodies in virtual reality; "ai amader Bangladesh," which features Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's lecture delivered on 7 March; and "The Grand Canyon," which describes the settlement clan Garikhad in North America's Grand Canyon that existed four thousand years ago. In addition, the planetarium introduced a new capsule simulator, a smart-step floor, and 3D video. In 2013, it also established a Nuclear Industrial Information Centre.
